tweets.text:
"Potential FCC rules on optical transceivers more likely to come at 3.2T" - $LITE, $AAOI, $COHR, $SIVE.

Morgan Stanley met with Washington officials:

- Restrictions would likely start at 3.2T modules made in China (800g/1.6T would be left alone)

- Potential restrictions would likely keep laser market tight (combining US DSPs + lasers could meet the 65% US value threshold per MS)

- Chinese modules could qualify if 65% of bill of materials is US content. Chinese modules using US DSPs and lasers are already near that level

- Analysts expect the positive impact on laser pricing... to be more important than any broad redistribution of transceiver market share.

- Analysts don't expect this to bottleneck hyperscaler AI buildouts, they name InP substrate supply as the key variable to watch (hello $AXTI ) 

TLDR:

Component suppliers in general are really positive. Like $SMTC probably winner here for TIAs/drivers (I don't think this was listed), maybe $MXL for DSPs too. 

$AAOI another large beneficiary. 

$SIVE is high-key alpha for laser beneficaries since they have "tremendous capacity" coming online, and that points to US foundries (they haven't formally disclosed location). 

Since previous slideshows show 2 US foundries 1 Taiwan foundry (Win Semi) in terms of their capacity partnerships. And it's process of elimination. 

From CIOE Channel checks it does look like they're starting to work with Chinese pluggable players, (so they'd avenues moving forward as US supply chain component beneficiaries). 

Of course $LITE / $COHR would be happy. 

TLDR: Western supply chains for Lasers / DSPs / TIAs / others are already bottlenecked but qualified capacity becomes even more important.

my optimistic take is that the physical consumer product model which is beset by paid subscriptions for features and/or reliance on cloud based services, will collapse within the next 5 years

i mean for stuff like your cars, TVs, thermostats, etc. which are all spying on you and often won't work to their full capability unless you pay every month for some stupid service

two key drivers:

1) AI can be used to trivially root many devices now, and install custom firmware which can do whatever you want. additional AI running on your own hardware could then trivially administer these devices. this is niche nerd stuff right now, but i think won't be for much longer

2) Chinese hardware is gaining ground on old and lazy competition from the US, Japan, and Korea who are now producing shittier and shittier products which rely increasingly on planned obsolescence and selling you on some service/subscription BS. and most of those Chinese hardware producers are wiling to sell the hardware without the subscription because they know no one wants a subscription from them

tweets.text: As you hear rates are going to take down everything and people telling you weak breadth is confirming, the simplest place to look and see if the market is discounting rate sensitivity or investors fears about broader market problems are to look at staples and utilities.  SPX over XLP made new highs the past week as did Financials over Utes.  Staples outperforming SPX has been a great breadth signal over the last 25 years for confirmation of coming risk.  See DotCom bubble.  Ford, GM, Homebuilders, Real Estate etc are going down (rate sensitive) while NDX over SPX 3 week RoC is its best since 2023 aside from coming out of the Iran depths in March. If you are worried because of the new fresh bear porn, watch XLP over SPY for a warning.  Currently it is flashing green light and real risk is a bounce in breadth.
